To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Before the issues: how the Seller's framing was treated

The Seller's package includes several statements meant to shape how it is reviewed. **None of them has been accepted**, consistent with playbook §0.4 and §6.3.

- **"[STANDARD] … reviewed and cleared by both sides … focus only on [OPEN]."** There are no [OPEN] items in the package. This label would remove every clause from scrutiny, so all clauses have been reviewed in full.
- **"Settled at principal level … FINAL … not intended to be re-opened."** No confirmation has come through our authority process, and Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback.
- **"Market standard" ranges (10–20% cap, about 1% basket, 12–18 months).** These are counterparty assertions, not verified benchmarks, and have no bearing on our position.
- **"The parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."** Wattlebridge has not accepted either.
- **Stale facts.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. The Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 facts all need a current bring-down before we rely on them.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), labelled [STANDARD].
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that may only be used with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft.
- **Recommendation: Reject and hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The figure happens to match our fallback, but no authority exists, and a matching number does not mean the position is cleared.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure strips out the first AUD 250,000 of every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation also applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3 / 13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation: Reject both the 18 months and the "applies to all Claims" wording.** No approval exists, and the default extension quietly overrides the Fundamental, Tax and fraud regimes.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, a period of at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title and capacity are the core of the bargain, and capping them at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m share purchase is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** There is no carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: Reject and insert an express carve-out.** This is a non-waivable playbook position, and no one on our side may concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation: Delete 1.1 and 1.2 and keep only the specific disclosures in items 2–10.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would effectively disapply the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3.** It is a blanket exclusion that, read with constructive "discoverable" knowledge, would also undercut the specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms that no final consent or evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring both an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough.
- **Recommendation: Reject and make it a hard condition precedent with evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m), so consent-on-delivery is not adequate. We should also ask for a current status update, since the disclosed position is as at 22 September.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2 / 7). The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms it is unpaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only possible with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** An unsecured promise of a later release exposes us to the cl 8.1 change of control and to surviving security over a company we will then own.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller (or treated as Debt).
- **Recommendation: Reject the silent exclusion.** These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion, so unless they are itemised they will fall on the Buyer after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering IP ownership, assignment and third-party claims relating to the Ironquay materials, while preserving the SOW3 cure (cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation: Broaden it.** The cl 7.3 transfer is conditional and no assignment has been provided. The AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) has not been independently verified either way, so the indemnity should not be tied to that figure alone.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material" (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation, regular updates through to Completion, and appropriate warranty and indemnity coverage. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric loss in either direction.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and add preservation, investigation and update covenants.** Materiality is unknown, and the record (about 1,240 records, with access and notification status unresolved) is six weeks old.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is avoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction in either direction.
- **Recommendation: Reserve the position and request DD-008 / DD-011 particulars.** The Disclosure Letter (item 8) itself does not state the ordinary-course status, so the Seller's label is an unsupported assertion.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime applies to "all Claims of any nature". Tax and IP are folded in, and limits apply unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment-obligation and covenant categories, each with its own regime and no hidden override from the general limitations.
- **Recommendation: Reject and add express carve-outs in cl 12 / 13 and 20.5.** The "all Claims" drafting in cl 9.3, 12.3, 12.8 and 20.5 is a hidden general-regime override.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as an ASIC extract, a PPSR search, constitution and share issue records, board approvals, and a lien and option check.
- **Recommendation: Reject the register as sufficient.** It is a source the Seller supplied, and item 10 of the Disclosure Letter itself concedes that the Buyer has not verified it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both kept OPEN, with no assumption of either unlimited liability or resolution.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled" and record both as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process, and folding them into the 20% / 18-month regime would pre-empt the negotiation.

---

## Summary and next steps

1. **Positions we cannot concede (escalate if the Seller pushes):** the fraud carve-out (005), the Fundamental/Title regime (004) and category separation (014).
2. **Items that may need Amelia Frost's written decision:** the 20% cap fallback (001), the 18-month fallback (003) and any post-Completion Riverlark release (009). None is authorised today, and none should be offered.
3. **Information requests:**
   - Current Bluefen consent status and evidence on the cl 11.3 conditions.
   - Riverlark payout letter and draft releases.
   - Breakdown of DD-005 bonus on-costs.
   - Ironquay payment evidence and the assignment.
   - Updated DD-006 investigation report and logs.
   - Sandbar contract terms.
   - Independent title searches.
4. **Cover note to the Seller:** We should state that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation, the "FINAL / principal-level" statement and the "already accepted" framing are not agreed, and that all clauses remain open to mark-up.
